**Part-A**
\
```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(ggplot2)
library(gridExtra)
library(tidyverse)
library(xts)
library(dlm)
```

```{r, message=FALSE, fig.align='center'}
sigma2v_tr <- 9
sigma2w_tr <- 4
m0_tr <- 0
C0_tr <- 25

data <- read.csv("DLM_data.csv")

y <- data$yt
t <- data$time

sim_data <- data.frame(y = y,
                       time = t)

gg_sim <- ggplot(sim_data,
                 aes(y = y,
                     x = time)) +
  geom_line(linetype = "dashed",
            color = "black") 

# construct a dlm model object #with parameters fixed at their true values
dlm_mod <- dlm(FF = 1.2,
               GG = 0.8,
               V = sigma2v_tr,
               W = sigma2w_tr,
               m0 = m0_tr,
               C0 = C0_tr)   

# filter the simulated data y using the dlm
sim_data_filtered <- dlmFilter(y = sim_data$y,
                               mod = dlm_mod)

# store and plot the one-step-ahead predictions 
# of theta and standard errors
sim_data$pred <- sim_data_filtered$a
sim_data$pSE <- sqrt(unlist(
  dlmSvd2var(sim_data_filtered$U.R, 
             sim_data_filtered$D.R)))
```
\newpage
```{r, fig.align='center'}
gg_sim +
  geom_line(data = sim_data, 
            aes(y = pred,
                x = time),
            color = "red",
            size = 1.2) +
  geom_ribbon(data = sim_data,
              aes(x = time, 
                  ymin = pred - 1.96 * pSE,
                  ymax = pred + 1.96 * pSE),
              fill = "red",
              alpha = 0.2) +
  labs(title = expression(
    paste("One-Step-Ahead Predictions of ",
          theta[t],
          " w/ Standard Errors"))) +
  ylab("")

a40 <- sim_data$pred[40]
R40 <- sim_data$pSE[40]^2

cat("The Numerical Value of a40 is: ", a40, "\n")
cat("The Numerical Value of R40 is: ", R40, "\n")

```

**Part-B**
\
```{r, message=FALSE, fig.align='center'}
data_dlm_2 <- sim_data
data_dlm_2$y_t <- 1.2 * sim_data$pred
data_dlm_2$qSE <- 1.2*1.2*sim_data$pSE^2 + 9

gg_sim +
  geom_line(data = data_dlm_2, 
            aes(y = y_t,
                x = time),
            color = "pink",
            size = 1.2) +
  geom_ribbon(data = data_dlm_2,
              aes(x = time, 
                  ymin = y_t - 1.96 * pSE,
                  ymax = y_t + 1.96 * pSE),
              fill = "pink",
              alpha = 0.2) +
  labs(title = expression(
    paste("One-Step-Ahead Predictions of ",
          y[t],
          " w/ Standard Errors"))) +
  ylab("")

f40 <- sim_data$pred[40]*1.2
Q40 <- sim_data$pSE[40]^2*1.2*1.2 + 9

cat("The Numerical Value of f40 is: ", f40, "\n")
cat("The Numerical Value of Q40 is: ", Q40, "\n")

```

**Part-C**
\
```{r, message=FALSE, fig.align='center'}
# Store and plot the filtering distribution  
# of theta
sim_data$filtered <- dropFirst(sim_data_filtered$m)
sim_data$fSE <- dropFirst(sqrt(unlist(
  dlmSvd2var(sim_data_filtered$U.C, 
             sim_data_filtered$D.C))))
gg_sim +
  geom_line(data = sim_data, 
            aes(y = pred,
                x = time),
            color = "red",
            size = .5) +
  geom_line(data = sim_data, 
            aes(y = filtered,
                x = time),
            color = "blue",
            size = 1.2) +
  geom_ribbon(data = sim_data,
              aes(x = time, 
                  ymin = filtered - 1.96 * fSE,
                  ymax = filtered + 1.96 * fSE),
              fill = "blue",
              alpha = 0.2) +
  labs(title = expression(
    paste("Mean of the filtering distribution of ",
          theta[t],
          " w/ Standard Errors"))) +
  ylab("")

y40 <- sim_data$y[40]
e40 <- y40 - f40

cat("The Numerical Value of m40 is: ", (a40) + (R40)*(1.2)*(e40)/(Q40), "\n")
cat("The Numerical Value of C40 is: ", (R40) - ((R40)^2)*(1.44)/(Q40), "\n")

```

**Part-E**
\
```{r, message=FALSE, fig.align='center'}
# store and plot the smoothed 
# predictions of theta and standard errors

sim_data_smoothed <- dlmSmooth(sim_data_filtered)
sim_data$smoothed <- dropFirst(sim_data_smoothed$s)
sim_data$sSE <- dropFirst(sqrt(unlist(
  dlmSvd2var(sim_data_smoothed$U.S, 
             sim_data_smoothed$D.S))))

gg_sim +
  geom_line(data = sim_data, 
            aes(y = pred,
                x = time),
            color = "red",
            size = .5) +
  geom_line(data = sim_data, 
            aes(y = filtered,
                x = time),
            color = "blue",
            size = .5) +
  geom_line(data = sim_data, 
            aes(y = smoothed,
                x = time),
            color = "darkgreen",
            size = 1.2) +
  geom_ribbon(data = sim_data,
              aes(x = time, 
                  ymin = smoothed - 1.96 * sSE,
                  ymax = smoothed + 1.96 * sSE),
              fill = "green",
              alpha = 0.2) +
  labs(title = expression(
    paste("Smoothed Values of ",
          theta[t],
          " w/ Standard Errors"))) +
  ylab("")

vals <- sim_data[is.na(sim_data$y), c('time', 'smoothed')]
cat("values of theta t, for the values of t such that yt is missing")
```

**Part-F**
\
```{r, message=FALSE, fig.align='center'}
forecast_ext <- dlmForecast(sim_data_filtered, nAhead = 10)
forecast_df <- data.frame(yt_forecast = forecast_ext$f,
                             time = seq(from = 101, to = 110),
                             Qt_forecast = unlist(forecast_ext$Q),
                             sSE = dropFirst(sqrt(unlist(
                               dlmSvd2var(sim_data_filtered$U.C, 
                                          sim_data_filtered$D.C)))))

ggplot(sim_data,
       aes(y = y,
           x = time)) +
  geom_line(color = "black")  + 
  geom_line(data = forecast_df, aes(x=time, y = yt_forecast), color = 'orange') +
  geom_ribbon(data = forecast_df,
              aes(x = time, 
                  ymin = yt_forecast - 1.96 * sqrt(Qt_forecast),
                  ymax = yt_forecast + 1.96 * sqrt(Qt_forecast)),
              fill = "orange",
              alpha = 0.2) +
  labs(title = expression(
    paste("Forecasted Values of ",
          y[101:110],
          " w/ Standard Errors"))) +
  ylab("")

q101 <- as.numeric(forecast_ext$Q[1])
q110 <- as.numeric(forecast_ext$Q[10])

cat("The Numerical Value of Q101 is: ", q101, "\n")
cat("The Numerical Value of Q110 is: ", q110, "\n")
```
\
A non-technical explanation for why the predictive variance of y101 may be less than that of y110 is that as you move further into the future, the uncertainty in the predictions increases. In the Kalman filter, the prediction variance accumulates over time due to the influence of the process noise (W) and measurement noise (V). Thus, the predictive variance tends to grow larger as we forecast further into the future.
